content.value_statement: Code changes can miss requirements, tests, and production risks. This skill provides a repeatable review workflow with clear severity levels.
actual_capabilities: Defines when developers should request a code review during a project.
Shows how to collect base and head git SHAs for review context.
Provides a structured reviewer prompt with requirements, git range, and checklist sections.
Separates findings into Critical, Important, and Minor severity groups.
Guides users to fix serious issues before continuing work.
Fits task-based, plan-based, and ad-hoc development workflows.
limitations: It does not run tests, linters, or security scanners by itself.
It depends on accurate requirements and valid git SHAs from the user.
Review quality depends on the reviewer model and available repository context.
It does not enforce merge policies or block deployment automatically.

use_cases.title: Feature Completion Review
use_cases.description: Request a focused review after finishing a feature and before starting the next task.

use_cases.title: Pre-Merge Quality Check
use_cases.description: Compare code changes with requirements and identify issues before merging to the main branch.

use_cases.title: Plan Execution Feedback
use_cases.description: Review batches of completed plan tasks to catch defects before they accumulate.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Latest Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request after a small task
prompt_templates.prompt: Request a code review for my latest completed task. Check whether it matches the requirements and identify any Critical, Important, or Minor issues.

prompt_templates.title: Review This Git Range
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with commit range context
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changes between my base and head commits. Compare them with the plan and give a clear merge readiness verdict.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Feature Before Merge
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this completed feature for architecture, error handling, tests, security concerns, and production readiness. Prioritize findings by severity.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Plan Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the completed task batch against the implementation plan. Identify missed requirements, regression risks, and fixes needed before the next batch.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for review after adding a verification function.
output_examples.output: The review lists strengths, one Important issue about missing progress feedback, one Minor cleanup item, and a ready-with-fixes assessment.

output_examples.input: A maintainer requests review before merging a feature branch.
output_examples.output: The review compares the work with requirements, calls out missing edge-case tests, recommends documentation updates, and gives a clear merge verdict.

output_examples.input: A team lead reviews a completed plan batch.
output_examples.output: The review confirms completed requirements, flags a compatibility risk, suggests a migration note, and recommends fixing it before continuing.

best_practices: Provide the reviewer with the implementation summary, requirements, and exact git range.
Fix Critical and Important findings before starting the next task.
Push back only with concrete code, tests, or requirement evidence.
anti_patterns: Requesting review without requirements or commit context.
Treating unclear feedback as accepted without asking for specifics.
Continuing development while important review findings remain unresolved.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you request structured code reviews with clear inputs, severity levels, and merge readiness guidance.

faq.question: Does it perform the review automatically?
faq.answer: It provides the workflow and reviewer prompt. A compatible AI tool or reviewer agent performs the actual review.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after major tasks, before merging, after complex bug fixes, or when you need a fresh technical review.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide what changed, the requirements, the base commit, the head commit, and a short implementation summary.

faq.question: Can it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. It improves review discipline, but teams should still use required human approvals where policy demands them.
